_readme: SEED FILE. `scripts/seed.ts` is the only code path that opens this
directory, and nothing here is read at runtime: Postgres is the
single source of truth once a row lands, so an edit below changes
nothing until the next seed pass applies it.
Keys beginning with an underscore are stripped by the loader before
anything is validated or written, which is what lets a seed file
carry this header at all. A seed is usually met on its own, in a
diff or an editor tab, where nothing about the content says which
path owns it.
This file seeds `domains`. A domain is upserted by `slug`, so a
second seed pass updates the same row rather than adding one; the
slug is the only key here that is not safe to rename.
`settings` is the DomainSettings payload declared in
`src/db/schema/domains.ts`. Every member of it is optional and an
absent member means the pipeline's own default applies, so a domain
configures only what it wants to differ. `findingsDisplayName` is
left out below for exactly that reason, and the example is complete
without it.
`example-tech-radar` is a worked example rather than a deployment.
It exists to show the shape of a domain and stays neutral about the
subject: the weights, the fields and the terms are illustrative,
not a recommendation. Real subject matter belongs to whoever
operates an instance and reaches the database through their own
seeds.
